newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Livshits - IMF accord ready to sign in about 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Livshits - IMF accord ready to sign in about 2 weeks.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits on Monday said that an agreement with the International Monetary Fund on a 1997 Russian economic plan would be ready to be signed in about two weeks.
"The agreement is at a rather high stage of readiness and at the moment we are in talks with the IMF mission, which is known to be in Moscow," he told a news conference.
Asked when he thought the agreement would be signed he said, "I don't know. Somewhere in the range of about two weeks."

Anton Siluanov, head of the Finance Ministry's Macroeconomic Department, told Reuters the mission would leave this week. He said the major differences between Russia and the IMF were over monthly breakdowns of revenues and the deficit.
The IMF wanted revenues and the deficit to be broken down evenly every month, which Russia opposes due to inconsistent tax collection, traditionally lowest at the start of the year.

Tax collection is one of Russia's most acute economic problems and the IMF repeatedly postponed tranches of its $10 billion, three-year loan to Russia last year, citing taxes. January and February tranches have not yet been paid.

Livshits said that March tax collection had improved slightly on February in rouble terms but that revenues had increased dramatically thanks to the successful launch last week of Russia's two billion mark Eurobond.

Tass news agency, citing Finance Ministry sources, said Livshits would lose his post as Finance Minister to First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, who would do both jobs in the cabinet being readied.

Siluanov said the IMF had put forward about 11 new terms for paying the tranches and had proposed the government take new steps to implement economic reforms before April, when the IMF's board of directors meets.
He said that Russia and the IMF had agreed 1997 budget revenues of about 304 trillion roubles ($53 billion) and a 180 trillion rouble budget deficit.

The figures are calculated according to IMF standards, which include wage and pension arrears in the deficit, he said, although Russian accounting includes those items under budget expenditures, he said.
